title: Adaptive comm-reservation and kernel hedging for token-wave scheduling
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Tail latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads spikes when large prefill waves saturate inter-GPU links, causing head-of-line blocking for low-latency decodes. Existing token-shard batching and static NCCL windows handle common cases but are brittle under bursty PLG traffic and heterogeneous device mixes.

Proposal: Implement 'token-wave' scheduling combined with adaptive comm-reservation and kernel hedging. A token-wave groups contiguous prefill/decode work arriving in a short time window; the scheduler exposes two runtime levers: (1) adaptive comm-reservation allocates short-duration NCCL/collective reservation windows sized to anticipated token-wave comm needs based on lightweight queue predictions, enabling overlap of comm and compute without wholesale global locking; (2) kernel hedging chooses between a low-latency fused-attention kernel and a high-throughput tiled-attention kernel per microbatch, launching a speculative hedged kernel on a spare stream when hedging conditions trigger.

Design details: The scheduler maintains a small rolling histogram of recent prefill sizes and decode latencies per model+shape to estimate reservation size. Reservation requests are soft (best-effort) and time-limited to avoid starving background throughput; if reservations fail, the scheduler falls back to opportunistic streaming with smaller microbatch sizes. Kernel hedging uses lightweight cost model: if predicted latency variance > threshold and a spare SM occupancy budget exists, spawn hedged kernel (low-latency variant) with cancellation of the other when one finishes. Hedging is gated by per-GPU hedging budget and an operator flag.

API/flags: new runtime flags --token_wave_window_ms, --comm_reservation_fraction, --enable_kernel_hedging. New telemetry tags: token_wave_id, comm_reservation_alloc_bytes, hedged_kernel_launched.

Trade-offs: Reservations can reduce aggregate throughput if oversized or mispredicted; hedging increases short-term GPU utilization and power but reduces tail latency. We prefer soft reservations and conservative hedging defaults.

Observability & rollout: Add dashboards for reservation success rate, hedging win-rate, and decode tail latency (p50/p95/p99). Start with an internal canary on dedicated pool with heterogeneous A100/V100 mixes, then gradual rollout to hosted low-traffic customers.

Testing & benchmarks: Microbenchmarks show ~28% p99 reduction on mixed prefill+decode synthetic workload (batch sizes 1-8) with a 6% throughput regression in worst-case sustained prefill-only runs. Nightly perf suite and an A/B compare job will run for 7 days before broader rollout.

Links: design doc and perf logs included below in 'docs'.
